name: Marie Curie
summary: Marie Curie discovered polonium and radium, pioneering radioactivity research.

name: Ada Lovelace
summary: Ada Lovelace is recognized for her pioneering work on Charles Babbage's early mechanical general-purpose computer, the Analytical Engine, creating the first algorithm intended for machine processing.

name: Alan Turing
summary: Alan Turing is best known for his work on theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence, including the Turing machine and Turing test.

name: Grace Hopper
summary: Grace Hopper developed the first compiler for a computer programming language, leading to COBOL's creation.

name: Nikola Tesla
summary: Nikola Tesla is best known for his contributions to the design of the modern alternating current (AC) electricity supply system.

name: Rosalind Franklin
summary: Rosalind Franklin's X-ray crystallography work was crucial in determining the double helix structure of DNA.

name: Hedy Lamarr
summary: Hedy Lamarr co-invented a frequency-hopping spread spectrum technology that laid groundwork for modern wireless communications.

name: Linus Pauling
summary: Linus Pauling discovered the structure of proteins and co-founded the field of molecular biology.

name: Katherine Johnson
summary: Katherine Johnson calculated trajectories for NASA's early space missions, including the Apollo moon landings.

name: John von Neumann
summary: John von Neumann is best known for his work on the mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics and his role in the development of the digital computer.

name: Claude Shannon
summary: Claude Shannon is best known for his 1937 thesis introducing information theory, laying the foundation for digital communication and computer science.

name: Tim Berners-Lee
summary: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989, revolutionizing global information sharing.

name: Donald Knuth
summary: Donald Knuth is renowned for creating the TeX typesetting system and popularizing the analysis of algorithms.

name: Edsger Dijkstra
summary: Edsger Dijkstra is best known for developing the shortest path algorithm, Dijkstra's algorithm.

name: Barbara Liskov
summary: Barbara Liskov is known for her work on object-oriented programming and her creation of the Liskov Substitution Principle.

name: Margaret Hamilton
summary: Margaret Hamilton led software development for NASA's Apollo moon landing program, creating real-time flight control software.

name: Vint Cerf
summary: Vint Cerf co-invented the TCP/IP protocol suite, foundational to the development of the internet.

name: Dennis Ritchie
summary: Dennis Ritchie is best known for co-inventing the C programming language in the early 1970s.

name: Ken Thompson
summary: Ken Thompson co-created Unix and developed the B and Go programming languages.

name: Fei-Fei Li
summary: Fei-Fei Li co-founded ImageNet, a database crucial for advancing computer vision and AI research.
